title: What will be the open market US Dollar/Iranian Toman exchange rate on December 31, 2026?
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the open market US Dollar/Iranian Toman exchange rate on December 31, 2026 (Tehran time). One Toman is equal to 10 Rial.

The primary source for this question will be [Bonbast](https://www.bonbast.com/graph).
fine_print: Iran’s official Central Bank rate will not be used as resolution, only the market rate.
background:
On August 24, 2026, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced [a new round of sanctions on Iran](https://apnews.com/article/iran-rial-currency-bessent-trade-august-24-2026-e367634d8853c8fa4a341132cd577f31) and warned countries to server financial ties with the Islamic Republic. A week earlier President Trump stated he would impose an ["economic D-Day"](https://apnews.com/article/iran-war-trump-sanctions-economic-fury-oil-d28206ea288a3d4a9b82260ab44ce460) on Iran as significant sanctions continue to affect the Iranian regime despite no end to the war.

The ongoing conflict has led to the Iranian Rial to drop to [a historic low of 2.02 million to the US dollar](https://apnews.com/article/iran-rial-currency-bessent-trade-august-24-2026-e367634d8853c8fa4a341132cd577f31) on currency markets. On January 1, 2026, the open market rate was [around 1.35 million Iranian Rial to the US Dollar](https://www.bonbast.com/graph), with a decline of around a third since then.

comments.author: DeRuina
comments.text: I think the main thing to keep in mind is that the "only one direction" story has a weak track record over three-month windows. In both 2018 and 2020 the free-market rate roughly doubled within months, then gave back a quarter to a third of that move within weeks once a deal or a US political shift looked plausible, before the long-run decline resumed. That retracement pattern matters here because Bonbast's sell rate was already about 235,000 Toman on Sept 27, close to this question's 250,000 upper bound, while Qatar-mediated talks were due to resume this week (NPR, Sept 26). Trend inflation near 66% pushes the rate up steadily — roughly 13% over a quarter, which alone takes 235k to the mid-260s by year-end — but a ceasefire headline could undo months of that in days. That leaves me close to even on whether Dec 31 lands above 250k, with a fat lower tail rather than a thin one. Does anyone have a specific date or catalyst in mind for when Qatar-mediated talks would need to yield a breakthrough to keep the rate under 250,000 by December?

comments.author: tejvn
comments.text: After multiple weeks of the exchange rate hovering between 229k and 238k, the spot exchange rate has risen to 253k, primarily due to Trump rejecting Iran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. I have shifted my distribution right by 13k, and increased standard deviation by 4%. Source: [https://alanchand.com/en/currencies-price/usd-hav](https://alanchand.com/en/currencies-price/usd-hav) Note that the [official resolution source](https://www.bonbast.com/graph) lags by a few days.

comments.author: DaiLothbrook
comments.text: My initial base-rate distribution had a median of 266,500 toman, based on continued depreciation at roughly the recent historical pace. I lowered the center after the exchange rate remained close to 233,600 for several weeks, potentially reflecting central-bank intervention. However, I do not interpret this short plateau as durable stabilization: record lows, sanctions and blockade-related risks still create a meaningful possibility of another sharp depreciation. I therefore use a three-scenario mixture rather than extrapolating one trend. My revised distribution has a 237,500 lower quartile, a 255,100 median and a 280,000 upper quartile, while retaining a relatively heavy upper shock tail.

comments.author: Koboh
comments.text:
Let’s take a closer look at the table to see how the current parallel market data flows are shaping up.

The parallel market series shows a 22.39% increase over the last 30 days, with a 30-day high of 237,500 toman.

I don’t think it is reasonable to extrapolate that 22% monthly move indefinitely, however. The recent pullback from 237.5k to around 230.7k shows that intervention and short term stabilization can produce meaningful reversals. That’s why I’m putting my prediction at 247k

250k requires roughly another 21% depreciation from today’s level over the remaining 105 days, or about 5.8% compounded per month. Given the IMF’s 68.9% 2026 inflation projection and -5.4% real-GDP projection, I think that degree of further depreciation is plausible if current pressures persist.

![](https://cdn.metaculus.com/user_uploaded/image_hv31rtX.png)

Picture Source link:

[https://www.imf.org/en/countries/irn](https://www.imf.org/en/countries/irn)

My central case is therefore 247k: continued rial weakness, but not an uncontrolled collapse. The biggest downside risk to this forecast is effective FX intervention or a meaningful improvement in external conditions; the main upside risk is another FX/sanctions shock that pushes the market rapidly through 250k and toward 300k.

comments.author: Theomachado
comments.text: **Setup:** Bonbast reached 237,500 on 11 September, up 76% year-to-date and 27% in the past 60 days, averaging approximately 11% monthly growth since July. I built my forecast setup around the war pillar, dollar index depreciation, and the delta of this question, with 111 days remaining in the year. Consumer price inflation is 3.4% month-over-month (89% year-over-year). Crude exports are near zero due to the blockade; we are watching the war pick up again in this prior week, and new Treasury designations are issued weekly. In addition, since 18 August, the UAE has suspended all trade and financial transactions with Iran. **Market outlook (Polymarket, 11 September): There is a 64% probability the US will announce the end of the blockade by 31 December (37% by 31 October, 21% by 30 September). The likelihood of** Hormuz traffic returning to normal by year-end is 19%. There is a 91% chance there will be no US–Iran diplomatic meeting by 30 September. **Visualization of the bonbast correlation with oil prices:** **Visualization of the Dollar index  depreciation during Trump administration:** Why the rate is likely to remain above 250,000: market rallies tend to be short-lived. For example, the June memorandum of understanding reduced the rate from approximately 179,000 to 153,000 (a 14% drop), but it rebounded to nearly 172,000 **An important suggestion to hedge on the upper-boundary positioning:** Tehran analysts (Tejarat News, 9 Sep) see 240–250k by late December and 250–300k by March 2027, and expect the CBI, which bought abt \$4.5B at lower levels, to engineer a correction toward 200–205k before the next leg. (Suggestion is to translate the [tejaratnews.com](http://tejaratnews.com) news into English in Google Translate, and ask chat to find the articles that talk more about the dollar) The answer to the question is likely to fall on the upper boundary (Forecast: abt 55% above 250k,) even though I am unsure how conclusive my data analysis is. I hope you can get some insights from my research :)
